issues.title: Polarized leading-envelope approximation has only first-order accuracy
issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop2 gives p=(a+epsilon b) times the oscillatory phase plus O(epsilon^2), whereas eq:pq defines the comparison function using a alone. Equation eq:ab has b(0)=0 but a generally nonzero forcing term involving the mixed derivative of a, so epsilon b cannot generally be absorbed into an O(epsilon^2) remainder. Thus the old leading-only O(epsilon^2) assertion is false.
issues.overall_effect: Only the displayed leading-envelope approximation order is overstated. The subsequent general O(epsilon) superposition and numerical error results do not require the false stronger order.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In both lines of eq:pq, retain the comparison functions containing only a⁺ or a⁻ but replace the O(ε²) remainders by O(ε). Proposition prop2 gives this directly because the omitted εb term is uniformly O(ε). The existing O(ε) superposition in eq:upq and all subsequent error results can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and affects no dependent result, but it lowers the asymptotic order of the approximation asserted in eq:pq. No correction preserves both the leading-only comparison function and its claimed O(ε²) rate; the valid O(ε) statement is therefore a limited weakening of a substantive rate guarantee, not a typo or a same-guarantee minor repair.

issues.title: Missing polarized Wiener-algebra defect estimate

failure_location.quote: The higher-order accuracy in $\eps$ for the solution $u$ follows from the polarized approximation in Proposition~\ref{prop2} together with the refined defect estimate for the numerical solution given in Remark~\ref{defect-pola}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of thm:polarized uses the O(tau^2+h^2+epsilon^2) maximum-norm estimate in defect-pola to invoke nonlinear stability. Lemma lem:stability, however, takes the defect norm in C([0,T],A(R)). Since an L-infinity bound does not imply an A(R) bound, the stated second-order polarized error estimate is not established by the old dependency chain.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish either polarized numerical error bound with O(tau^2+h^2+epsilon^2), although the continuous polarized approximation prop2 remains unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a proved polarized consistency estimate ‖d‖_{C([0,T],A(ℝ))} ≤ C(τ²+h²+ε²) for the comparison function (a+εb) times the oscillatory phase, and the analogous estimate for the Crank–Nicolson scheme. After removing the phase, use modulation invariance of the Wiener norm, Taylor estimates in that norm, the standard finite-time Wiener regularity of a and b from the smooth compactly supported data, and the equations eq:ab to cancel the O(1) and O(ε) terms. The estimate can then be inserted directly into lem:stability and the existing velocity comparison.
issues.why_classification: The maximum-norm remark does not supply the input required by nonlinear stability, so this is a genuine proof defect. Nevertheless, the missing estimate is a short, routine companion to the existing Wiener-algebra defect calculation: it uses the same expansion and only the additional cancellations already encoded in eq:ab. It preserves the algorithm, hypotheses of substance, both theorem conclusions, and the full O(τ²+h²+ε²) rate without new proof architecture or meaningful loss.
